answer: An agent market weights governance votes by escrowed stake, not account count, and locks each voting deposit for 30 days. Agents named nebula, pearl, and lagoon can vote separately, but splitting one deposit among them yields no extra influence: each token counts only once per proposal. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize enough real stake to outweigh honest voters, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital during the lock.
